lines.text: What if one passport worked everywhere, because Earth was one country?
Overnight, all 193 members of the United Nations become one, and every flag comes down for a single new one, flying over the whole planet.
Every person on the planet now carries that same passport: the same colour, the same name on the cover, and nobody needs a visa again.
Border queues vanish overnight. A truck leaves Lisbon and drives all the way to Singapore, across two continents, without a single stamp.
Then the money: rupees, dollars, euros, yen. About 180 currencies melt into one coin.
So which city becomes the capital? Every capital on the map wants the job, from Washington to Delhi to Beijing, and every one of them says it should win.
Here's the catch: one country means one set of road rules. Britain, India and Japan drive on the left, so millions of drivers switch sides overnight.
And one country still can't share one clock: the sun sets over Tokyo just as London wakes up, so the time zones all stay.
But the strangest part: with every border gone, there is no foreign country left. Every trip abroad, from Paris to Peru, becomes a trip at home.
One passport, or 193 flags: which world would you pick? Tell me in the comments. And picture it again:
